slides.head:
China's first all-AI film booked
10,000 screenings. Not the seats.
Two years, 100 people.
slides.body: Sanxingdui: Future Past, a sci-fi thriller from Bona Film Group, is billed as China's first fully AI-generated feature film. Nearly 100 people spent more than two years on it. Budget: more than 10 million yuan, about $1.5 million.

slides.head: 10,000 screenings. Four seats.
slides.body: It opened on October 23 with more than 10,000 screenings scheduled, according to ticketing platform Maoyan. At the screening AFP attended, four people sat in the room.

slides.head: $43,000 against $1.5 million.
slides.body: By Friday evening the film had taken close to 290,000 yuan, about $43,000. Maoyan forecasts a final total near 390,000 yuan. That is under 4 percent of what it cost to make.

slides.head: The same AI wins on phones.
slides.body: AI-generated short dramas on Douyin, China's TikTok, drew more than 200 billion views in September alone. Audiences accept AI in the feed. They have not paid for it in a cinema.

slides.head:
Free scrolls.
Tickets are earned.
slides.body: The tools can now carry a feature. The audience still buys a reason to leave the house. Spend the AI budget on the story and the craft, not on proving the pipeline works.
